Wrangling Messy Csv Files By Detecting Row And Type Patterns

Wrangling Messy CSV Files by Detecting Row and Type Patterns

Their parsing method is able to get 97% accuracy with dialect detection.

Intro

There are 39 different possible dialects, just within CSV files alone. And data can be separated by commas, semicolons, spaces, tabs, or other characters.

Parsing CSVs is an open CS problem and the bets tools out there still have issues parsing dialects accurately regularly.

Problem State

Let:

  • Σ\SigmaΣ (sigma) = finite alphabet of characters in an encoding
  • EEE (epsilon) = the encoding
  • Σ∗\Sigma{^*}Σ∗ = all possible strings in the alphabet Σ\SigmaΣ
  • A csv file is therefore an element xxx such that x∈Σ∗x \in \Sigma^*x∈Σ∗
  • A csv file contains NNN tuples tit_iti​ that are elements of a product set
  • ti∈V1×V2×⋯×VLit_i \in V_1 \times V_2 \times \cdots \times V_{L_i}ti​∈V1​×V2​×⋯×VLi​​ , where VjV_jVj​ is the domains of values of tuples.
    • tuple: fininite sequence (ordered list)
  • All tuples in a file is contained in TTT where T=[t1,⋯ ,tN]T = [t_1, \cdots, t_N ]T=[t1​,⋯,tN​]
  • θ\thetaθ is the dialect of the CSV file
  • The formatter first:
    • converts the data TTT to a string representation CCC where the domains in the tuples are string domain (Σ∗\Sigma^*Σ∗)
  • Then stage two: 
    - the string representation is converted to CSV file $x$
    Unfortunately retrieving the information from the CSV file loses the dialect and formatter information.

For the dialect, given a csv file xxx:

  • x∈Σ∗x \in \Sigma^*x∈Σ∗
  • θ\thetaθ is the dialect, which is the parameters needed to map the tuples C=[c1,⋯ ,cN]C = [c_1, \cdots, c_N]C=[c1​,⋯,cN​] to the file xxx
  • fθ(C)=xf_\theta(C) = xfθ​(C)=x
  • fθf_\thetafθ​ represents stage 2 of the formatter, converting the file back would therefore be fθ−1(x)=Cf_\theta^{-1}(x) = Cfθ−1​(x)=C
  • function ggg is used in stage 1 to convert data to the string representation g(T)=Cg(T) = Cg(T)=C, therefore inversely returning the string to the data is g−1(C)=Tg^{-1}(C) = Tg−1(C)=T

A consistency measure for dialect detection

If the csv is parsed correctly the tuples will be more consistent than if not.

The dialect θ\thetaθ consists of three parameters:

  • θd\theta_dθd​ = delimiter
  • θq\theta_qθq​ = quote character
  • θe\theta_eθe​ = escape character Each parameter can be a single character or absent (ϵ\epsilonϵ).

The consistency score for a given dialect is:

Q(x,θ)=P(x,θ)⋅T(x,θ)Q(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta}) = P(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta}) \cdot T(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta})Q(x,θ)=P(x,θ)⋅T(x,θ)
  • PPP = pattern score
  • TTT = type score
  • QQQ = consistency score
  • Θx\Theta_{\mathbf{x}}Θx​ = set of potential dialects The dialect with the highest consistency score is selected:
θ^=arg⁡max⁡θ∈ΘxQ(x,θ)\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} = \arg\max_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\in\Theta_{\mathbf{x}}} Q(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta})θ^=argθ∈Θx​max​Q(x,θ)

4.1 Pattern Score

Abstract each row into a pattern, ignoring cell contents but accounting for quotes and escape characters.

  • CCC = cell
  • DDD = delimiter
  • KKK = number of distinct row patterns
  • NkN_kNk​ = number of occurrences of pattern kkk
  • LkL_kLk​ = number of cells in pattern kkk

The pattern score is calculated as:

P(x,θ)=1K∑k=1KNkLk−1LkP(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}N_k\frac{L_k-1}{L_k}P(x,θ)=K1​k=1∑K​Nk​Lk​Lk​−1​

The score favors:

  • Fewer distinct patterns.
  • More frequently occurring patterns.
  • Patterns with more columns.

To prevent single-column files from receiving a score of zero, introduce α=10−3\alpha=10^{-3}α=10−3:

P(x,θ)=1K∑k=1KNkmax⁡(α,Lk−1)LkP(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}N_k\frac{\max(\alpha,L_k-1)}{L_k}P(x,θ)=K1​k=1∑K​Nk​Lk​max(α,Lk​−1)​

Uninterpreted quote characters can also distinguish otherwise identical row patterns.

4.2 Type Score

Determine the proportion of cells matching recognizable data types.

  • T\mathcal{T}T = set of recognized data types
  • μ(z)\mu(z)μ(z) = function identifying the type of string zzz
  • MMM = total number of parsed cells
  • NNN = number of rows
  • LiL_iLi​ = number of cells in row iii
  • ci,jc_{i,j}ci,j​ = cell at row iii, column jjj
  • III = indicator function (1 if true, 0 otherwise)
T(x,θ)=1M∑i=1N∑j=1LiI[μ(ci,j)∈T]T(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{L_i}I[\mu(c_{i,j})\in\mathcal{T}]T(x,θ)=M1​i=1∑N​j=1∑Li​​I[μ(ci,j​)∈T]

Recognized types include:

  • Empty cells
  • Numbers
  • URLs and email addresses
  • Percentages and currencies
  • Dates and times
  • Alphanumeric strings

Types are identified using regular expressions.

To prevent unrecognized data types from reducing the entire consistency score to zero:

T~(x,θ)=max⁡(β,T(x,θ))\tilde{T}(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \max(\beta,T(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\theta}))T~(x,θ)=max(β,T(x,θ))

Where β=10−10\beta=10^{-10}β=10−10.

Note: type score evaluates individual cells, not type consistency within columns.

4.3 Tie Breaking

If multiple dialects have the same consistency score:

  • Determine whether the differing dialect parameter affects the parsed result.
  • If removing a parameter produces identical data, prefer its absence.
  • Apply this to delimiters, quote characters and escape characters.

4.4 Potential Dialects

Generate potential dialects from characters present in the file rather than evaluating every possible character combination.

  • D\mathcal{D}D = potential delimiters
  • Q\mathcal{Q}Q = potential quote characters
  • Ed,q\mathcal{E}_{d,q}Ed,q​ = potential escape characters for a delimiter-quote combination

Algorithm 2: Construction of Potential Dialects

  1. Filter URLs from the input to avoid detecting their punctuation as delimiters.
  2. Identify potential delimiters using Unicode character categories and an exclusion list.
  3. Identify potential quote characters from an allowed set.
  4. Identify potential escape characters:
    • Must belong to Unicode category Po (Other Punctuation).
    • Must occur immediately before a potential delimiter or quote character.
  5. Include absent parameters (ϵ\epsilonϵ) as candidates.
  6. Generate combinations of delimiters, quote characters and their corresponding escape characters.
  7. Reject dialects whose delimiter is always contained within quoted sections.
  8. Return the remaining potential dialects.

noteIndex.body:
![](/assets/images/allard-lab.jpg)

Welcome the the COMMONS Lab Open Dendron !

In the [COMMONS Lab](https://www.unifr.ch/bio/en/groups/allard/) we intent to follow the [Open Notebook Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-notebook_science) approach to document our research.

For this we use the [Dendron](https://www.dendron.so/) system as a mean to efficiently capture notes and publish them.

## What is this note

This note is a succinct tutorial note aiming to get you started in the use of the COMMONS Lab Dendron.

## Tutorial

### Dendron. 

#### What is Dendron ?

> Dendron is an open-source, local-first, markdown-based, note-taking tool. Think of it as a cache for everything that you care about - if you've spent more then five minutes solving a problem, you should never spent any more time solving the same exact problem.
> 
> Dendron is a knowledge base built by and for developers and integrates natively with IDEs like VS Code and VSCodium.

#### Where to get more info on Dendron ?

- You can get more information in the Dendron system at the official website www.dendron.so
- All the Dendron documentation is hosted here https://wiki.dendron.so/. It is, obviously, a Dendron itself.

#### Concrete steps to access and contribute to the DBGI Dendron

1. Install [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/download)
2. Install [Dendron](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=dendron.dendron) from the VSCode marketplace 
3. Clone the COMMONS Dendron repo

    In your terminal
    ```
    git clone https://github.com/commons-research/commons-dws-public.git
    ```
4. In VSCode open (File/Open) the cloned repository.
5. Voila ! You should now be in the COMMONS Lab Open Dendron.

Feel free to explore and contribute.
A first, important step could be to configure VSCode so that you can easily add a daily note. See steps described at [[open-notebook.commons.setup]]


## Questions, comments, suggestions ?

Feel free to contribute here https://github.com/orgs/commons-research/discussions
